mcq_options.text: Scarcity of resources relative to wants

items.prompt:
The fundamental economic problem faced by every society arises from:

A) Scarcity of resources relative to wants
B) Too much money in circulation
C) A shortage of government ministries
D) An excess of factories
items.correct_answer: A) Scarcity of resources relative to wants

items.prompt:
Human wants are best described as:

A) Strictly limited
B) Unlimited
C) Always satisfied
D) Fixed by law

mcq_options.text: Allocates scarce resources among competing wants

items.prompt:
Economics is best defined as the study of how society:

A) Prints its national currency
B) Trains its armed forces
C) Allocates scarce resources among competing wants
D) Writes its constitution
items.correct_answer: C) Allocates scarce resources among competing wants

mcq_options.text: Commands a price because it is scarce

items.prompt:
A resource is described as economic (rather than free) when it:

A) Is supplied by the government
B) Is found only underground
C) Is used only by firms
D) Commands a price because it is scarce
items.correct_answer: D) Commands a price because it is scarce

items.prompt:
Which of the following is a free good in most situations?

A) Air for breathing
B) Petrol
C) Land in a city centre
D) Clean piped water

mcq_options.text: The money spent on a good

items.prompt:
Opportunity cost refers to:

A) The money spent on a good
B) The next best alternative forgone
C) The total cost of production
D) A tax paid to government
items.correct_answer: B) The next best alternative forgone

mcq_options.text: The price of a cinema ticket
The enjoyment of the film forgone

items.prompt:
A student who chooses to read for an exam instead of watching a film has an opportunity cost equal to:

A) The price of a cinema ticket
B) The cost of the textbooks
C) The enjoyment of the film forgone
D) Zero, because reading is free
items.correct_answer: C) The enjoyment of the film forgone

items.prompt:
A government that builds a hospital instead of a stadium with the same funds incurs an opportunity cost of:

A) The total tax collected
B) The wages of the builders
C) The interest on its debt
D) The stadium forgone

mcq_options.text: The amount of one good given up to get more of another
The total output of both goods

items.prompt:
On a production possibility curve, opportunity cost is shown by:

A) The amount of one good given up to get more of another
B) The total output of both goods
C) The point of maximum unemployment
D) The distance from the origin
items.correct_answer: A) The amount of one good given up to get more of another

items.prompt:
A point lying inside (below) a production possibility curve indicates that resources are:

A) Fully and efficiently employed
B) Under-utilised or inefficiently used
C) Unobtainable with current resources
D) Owned by the government

A point lying outside a production possibility curve is:

A) A position of full employment
B) A position of unemployment
C) Unattainable with current resources
D) The most efficient point

An outward shift of the whole production possibility curve usually represents:

A) A fall in total output
B) Rising unemployment
C) Higher inflation
D) Economic growth

The typical production possibility curve is bowed outward because of:

A) Increasing opportunity cost
B) Constant opportunity cost
C) Zero opportunity cost
D) Falling opportunity cost

In a free-market (capitalist) economy, the main allocator of resources is:

A) The central planning board
B) The price mechanism
C) The army
D) The trade unions

An economy in which the government owns and directs most resources is called a:

A) Free-market economy
B) Subsistence economy
C) Planned (command) economy
D) Barter economy

An economy that combines private enterprise with government participation is a:

A) Pure capitalist economy
B) Pure socialist economy
C) Closed economy
D) Mixed economy

Which question is NOT one of the basic economic questions every society must answer?

A) Who should win the election
B) What to produce
C) How to produce
D) For whom to produce
items.correct_answer: A) Who should win the election

mcq_options.text: Guarantees an equal income for everyone
Allocates resources through consumer choice and competition

items.prompt:
A major advantage claimed for the free-market system is that it:

A) Guarantees an equal income for everyone
B) Allocates resources through consumer choice and competition
C) Eliminates all unemployment
D) Removes the need for money
items.correct_answer: B) Allocates resources through consumer choice and competition

mcq_options.text: Backed by the ability and willingness to pay

items.prompt:
Effective demand differs from a mere want because it is:

A) Always satisfied by the state
B) Limited to luxury goods
C) Backed by the ability and willingness to pay
D) Independent of price
items.correct_answer: C) Backed by the ability and willingness to pay

items.prompt:
Goods that satisfy human wants directly, such as food and clothing, are called:

A) Capital goods
B) Free goods
C) Public goods
D) Consumer goods

Machines and tools used to produce other goods are classified as:

A) Capital goods
B) Consumer goods
C) Free goods
D) Inferior goods

A list of wants arranged in order of their importance is called a:

A) Demand schedule
B) Scale of preference
C) Budget line
D) Production schedule

mcq_options.text: Limited income relative to many wants

items.prompt:
The main reason a consumer must draw up a scale of preference is:

A) Government regulation
B) A surplus of money
C) Limited income relative to many wants
D) The abundance of goods
items.correct_answer: C) Limited income relative to many wants

items.prompt:
The three central problems of what, how and for whom to produce all arise directly from:

A) Inflation
B) Taxation
C) International trade
D) Scarcity

mcq_options.text: Real alternatives forgone, not just money spent
The market price of the chosen good

items.prompt:
Opportunity cost is best measured in terms of:

A) Real alternatives forgone, not just money spent
B) The market price of the chosen good
C) The total revenue of firms
D) The rate of interest
items.correct_answer: A) Real alternatives forgone, not just money spent

items.prompt:
The law of demand states that, other things being equal, as the price of a good rises its quantity demanded:

A) Rises
B) Falls
C) Stays the same
D) Becomes zero

A normal demand curve slopes:

A) Upward from left to right
B) Vertically
C) Downward from left to right
D) Horizontally
items.correct_answer: C) Downward from left to right

items.prompt:
A movement along a demand curve caused by a change in the good's own price is called a:

A) Change in demand
B) Shift in demand
C) Change in supply
D) Change in quantity demanded

A rightward shift of the whole demand curve is described as:

A) An increase in demand
B) A decrease in demand
C) A fall in quantity demanded
D) A movement along the curve

For a normal good, a rise in consumers' income will:

A) Decrease demand
B) Leave demand unchanged
C) Increase demand
D) Make the good free

For an inferior good, a rise in consumers' income will:

A) Increase demand
B) Leave demand unchanged
C) Raise its price only
D) Decrease demand

Two goods that are jointly demanded, such as cars and petrol, have demand that is:

A) Complementary (joint)
B) Competitive (substitute)
C) Derived only
D) Composite

The demand for labour, which depends on the demand for the goods it makes, is an example of:

A) Joint demand
B) Derived demand
C) Composite demand
D) Competitive demand

The law of supply states that, other things being equal, as price rises the quantity supplied:

A) Falls
B) Stays the same
C) Disappears
D) Rises

A normal supply curve slopes:

A) Upward from left to right
B) Downward from left to right
C) Horizontally
D) Vertically
items.correct_answer: A) Upward from left to right

mcq_options.text: A shift of the supply curve
A movement along the supply curve
A shift of the demand curve

items.prompt:
A change in the quantity supplied caused by the good's own price is shown by:

A) A shift of the supply curve
B) A movement along the supply curve
C) A shift of the demand curve
D) A vertical demand curve
items.correct_answer: B) A movement along the supply curve

items.prompt:
A fall in the cost of raw materials will normally cause the supply curve to:

A) Shift to the left
B) Become vertical
C) Shift to the right
D) Slope downward

An increase in indirect taxes on a good will normally cause its supply curve to:

A) Shift to the right
B) Stay unchanged
C) Become horizontal
D) Shift to the left

Market equilibrium price is established where:

A) Demand is greater than supply
B) Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied
C) Supply is greater than demand
D) Price is fixed by government
items.correct_answer: B) Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied

items.prompt:
When the market price is above the equilibrium price there will be a:

A) Shortage (excess demand)
B) New equilibrium at once
C) Surplus (excess supply)
D) Rise in demand

When the market price is below the equilibrium price there will be a:

A) Surplus (excess supply)
B) Fall in demand
C) Rise in supply
D) Shortage (excess demand)

mcq_options.text: A higher price and larger quantity
A lower price and smaller quantity
A lower price and larger quantity

items.prompt:
If demand increases while supply is unchanged, the new equilibrium will show:

A) A higher price and larger quantity
B) A lower price and smaller quantity
C) The same price and quantity
D) A lower price and larger quantity
items.correct_answer: A) A higher price and larger quantity

mcq_options.text: A higher price and smaller quantity
A lower price and larger quantity
A higher price and larger quantity

items.prompt:
If supply increases while demand is unchanged, the new equilibrium will show:

A) A higher price and smaller quantity
B) A lower price and larger quantity
C) The same price and quantity
D) A higher price and larger quantity
items.correct_answer: B) A lower price and larger quantity

items.prompt:
A government-fixed maximum price set below the equilibrium price is called a:

A) Price floor
B) Equilibrium price
C) Price ceiling
D) Market price

A minimum price set above the equilibrium price, such as a minimum wage, is a:

A) Price ceiling
B) Subsidy
C) Market price
D) Price floor

mcq_options.text: A shortage and possible black market

items.prompt:
A maximum price (ceiling) on a staple food set below equilibrium is most likely to cause:

A) A shortage and possible black market
B) A surplus of the food
C) An automatic fall in demand
D) A rise in supply
items.correct_answer: A) A shortage and possible black market

items.prompt:
The satisfaction a consumer derives from consuming a good is called:

A) Profit
B) Utility
C) Revenue
D) Interest

The law of diminishing marginal utility states that, as more of a good is consumed, the extra satisfaction from each additional unit:

A) Rises
B) Stays constant
C) Falls
D) Becomes infinite

Price elasticity of demand measures the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in:

A) Income
B) Taste
C) Population
D) Price

Demand is said to be price elastic when the elasticity coefficient is:

A) Greater than one
B) Equal to zero
C) Equal to one
D) Less than one

Demand is said to be price inelastic when the elasticity coefficient is:

A) Greater than one
B) Less than one
C) Equal to one
D) Infinite

A perfectly inelastic demand curve is drawn as a line that is:

A) Horizontal
B) Downward sloping
C) Vertical
D) Upward sloping

A perfectly elastic demand curve is drawn as a line that is:

A) Vertical
B) Upward sloping
C) Bowed outward
D) Horizontal

If a 10% rise in price causes a 20% fall in quantity demanded, the price elasticity of demand is:

A) 2.0
B) 0.5
C) 0.2
D) 10

If a 20% rise in price causes a 10% fall in quantity demanded, the price elasticity of demand is:

A) 2.0
B) 0.5
C) 10
D) 0.1

When the price of a good rises by 5% and quantity demanded falls by 5%, the price elasticity of demand is:

A) 0 (perfectly inelastic)
B) Infinite
C) 5
D) 1 (unit elastic)

If a 25% fall in price leaves quantity demanded completely unchanged, demand is:

A) Perfectly inelastic (elasticity = 0)
B) Perfectly elastic
C) Unit elastic
D) Elastic with elasticity = 25

If demand for a good is price elastic, a fall in its price will cause total revenue to:

A) Fall
B) Rise
C) Stay the same
D) Become zero

If demand for a good is price inelastic, a rise in its price will cause total revenue to:

A) Fall
B) Stay the same
C) Rise
D) Become negative

Demand for a good with many close substitutes tends to be:

A) Inelastic
B) Perfectly inelastic
C) Zero
D) Elastic

Demand for a necessity such as salt tends to be:

A) Inelastic
B) Elastic
C) Perfectly elastic
D) Infinite

Demand for a good that takes up a very large share of a consumer's income tends to be:

A) Perfectly inelastic
B) More elastic
C) Unit elastic
D) Zero

Income elasticity of demand measures the responsiveness of demand to a change in:

A) The good's own price
B) The price of substitutes
C) Consumer income
D) Government policy

A good with a negative income elasticity of demand is classified as:

A) A normal good
B) A luxury good
C) A Giffen-free good
D) An inferior good

If a 10% rise in income leads to a 5% rise in demand, the income elasticity of demand is:

A) 0.5
B) 2.0
C) 5
D) 0.05

A positive cross elasticity of demand between two goods indicates that they are:

A) Complements
B) Substitutes
C) Unrelated
D) Both inferior

A negative cross elasticity of demand between two goods indicates that they are:

A) Substitutes
B) Unrelated
C) Complements
D) Both luxuries

Price elasticity of supply measures the responsiveness of quantity supplied to a change in:

A) Income
B) Advertising
C) Taste
D) Price

If a 10% rise in price causes a 30% rise in quantity supplied, the price elasticity of supply is:

A) 3.0
B) 0.33
C) 0.3
D) 10

mcq_options.text: The time period is very short

items.prompt:
Supply tends to be more elastic when:

A) The time period is very short
B) The time period is longer
C) The good cannot be stored
D) Factors of production are fixed
items.correct_answer: B) The time period is longer

items.prompt:
Which of the following is NOT a factor of production?

A) Land
B) Labour
C) Capital
D) Money

The reward for the factor of production 'land' is:

A) Rent
B) Wages
C) Interest
D) Profit

The reward for the factor of production 'labour' is:

A) Rent
B) Wages
C) Interest
D) Profit

The reward for the factor of production 'capital' is:

A) Rent
B) Wages
C) Interest
D) Profit

The reward for the entrepreneur, who bears risk and organises production, is:

A) Wages
B) Rent
C) Interest
D) Profit

All natural resources such as minerals, forests and rivers are classified under:

A) Land
B) Capital
C) Labour
D) Enterprise

Man-made aids to production such as machines and factories are classified as:

A) Land
B) Capital
C) Labour
D) Enterprise

The ease with which workers can move from one occupation to another is called:

A) Geographical mobility of labour
B) Division of labour
C) Occupational mobility of labour
D) Productivity of labour

The movement of workers from one place to another in search of jobs is called:

A) Occupational mobility of labour
B) Specialisation
C) Capital widening
D) Geographical mobility of labour

mcq_options.text: Splitting production into specialised tasks done by different workers
Paying all workers the same wage
Producing every good in one factory

items.prompt:
Division of labour means:

A) Splitting production into specialised tasks done by different workers
B) Sharing profit equally among workers
C) Paying all workers the same wage
D) Producing every good in one factory
items.correct_answer: A) Splitting production into specialised tasks done by different workers

mcq_options.text: Removes the need for any machinery
Increases output through specialisation and skill

items.prompt:
A major advantage of the division of labour is that it:

A) Removes the need for any machinery
B) Increases output through specialisation and skill
C) Guarantees full employment
D) Eliminates the need for trade
items.correct_answer: B) Increases output through specialisation and skill

items.prompt:
A disadvantage of the division of labour is that it can lead to:

A) Lower total output
B) Loss of all worker skills
C) Monotony and boredom for workers
D) An end to specialisation
items.correct_answer: C) Monotony and boredom for workers

items.prompt:
Production that extracts raw materials directly from nature, such as mining and farming, is called:

A) Secondary production
B) Tertiary production
C) Joint production
D) Primary production

Manufacturing and construction, which turn raw materials into finished goods, are examples of:

A) Secondary production
B) Primary production
C) Tertiary production
D) Direct production

The provision of services such as banking, teaching and transport is classified as:

A) Primary production
B) Tertiary production
C) Secondary production
D) Subsistence production

mcq_options.text: Long run, when all factors vary
Short run, when at least one factor is fixed

items.prompt:
The law of diminishing returns operates in the:

A) Long run, when all factors vary
B) Very long run only
C) Short run, when at least one factor is fixed
D) Period of perfect competition only
items.correct_answer: C) Short run, when at least one factor is fixed

items.prompt:
The law of diminishing returns states that as more of a variable factor is added to a fixed factor, marginal output will eventually:

A) Rise without limit
B) Stay constant
C) Become negative at once
D) Fall

mcq_options.text: At least one factor of production is fixed

items.prompt:
Diminishing returns is a short-run concept because it assumes that:

A) At least one factor of production is fixed
B) All factors are variable
C) Output is constant
D) Prices are fixed by government
items.correct_answer: A) At least one factor of production is fixed

items.prompt:
When all factors of production are increased and output increases by a greater proportion, the firm experiences:

A) Diminishing returns
B) Increasing returns to scale
C) Constant returns to scale
D) Decreasing returns to scale

Economies of scale refer to the fall in:

A) Total cost as output falls
B) Price as demand rises
C) Average cost as output increases
D) Wages as employment rises
items.correct_answer: C) Average cost as output increases

items.prompt:
The cost advantages a firm gains from buying raw materials in bulk are an example of:

A) External economies of scale
B) Diseconomies of scale
C) Diminishing returns
D) Internal economies of scale

Economies enjoyed by all firms in an industry because the industry as a whole grows are called:

A) External economies of scale
B) Internal economies of scale
C) Diseconomies of scale
D) Constant returns

mcq_options.text: The total output of the firm

items.prompt:
Productivity of labour is best measured as:

A) Total wages paid
B) Output per worker per period
C) The number of workers employed
D) The total output of the firm
items.correct_answer: B) Output per worker per period

items.prompt:
Specialisation will generally increase output only if it is accompanied by:

A) A fall in demand
B) Higher taxation
C) Exchange or trade
D) A ban on imports

Costs that do not change with the level of output in the short run are called:

A) Variable costs
B) Marginal costs
C) Average costs
D) Fixed costs

Costs that change directly with the level of output are called:

A) Variable costs
B) Fixed costs
C) Sunk costs
D) Average costs

Which of the following is an example of a fixed cost for a factory?

A) Cost of raw materials
B) Rent of the factory building
C) Wages of casual workers
D) Electricity used by machines
items.correct_answer: B) Rent of the factory building

mcq_options.text: Total fixed cost plus total variable cost

items.prompt:
Total cost is equal to:

A) Total revenue minus profit
B) Average cost minus marginal cost
C) Total fixed cost plus total variable cost
D) Fixed cost minus variable cost
items.correct_answer: C) Total fixed cost plus total variable cost

items.prompt:
If total fixed cost is N100 and total variable cost at an output of 10 units is N200, total cost is:

A) N100
B) N200
C) N2,000
D) N300

Average cost is calculated as:

A) Total cost divided by output
B) Total cost multiplied by output
C) Total revenue divided by output
D) Marginal cost divided by output
items.correct_answer: A) Total cost divided by output

items.prompt:
If total cost is N300 at an output of 10 units, the average cost is:

A) N3
B) N30
C) N300
D) N3,000

With total fixed cost of N100 at an output of 10 units, the average fixed cost is:

A) N100
B) N1,000
C) N10
D) N1

mcq_options.text: Total revenue from one more unit
Addition to total cost from producing one more unit

items.prompt:
Marginal cost is best defined as the:

A) Total cost divided by output
B) Cost of fixed factors only
C) Total revenue from one more unit
D) Addition to total cost from producing one more unit
items.correct_answer: D) Addition to total cost from producing one more unit

items.prompt:
If total cost rises from N300 to N330 when output rises from 10 to 11 units, the marginal cost of the 11th unit is:

A) N30
B) N3
C) N330
D) N300

Total revenue is calculated as:

A) Price divided by quantity
B) Price multiplied by quantity sold
C) Total cost plus profit
D) Quantity divided by price
items.correct_answer: B) Price multiplied by quantity sold

items.prompt:
If a firm sells 20 units at a price of N5 each, its total revenue is:

A) N25
B) N4
C) N100
D) N15

mcq_options.text: Total revenue divided by quantity sold

items.prompt:
Average revenue is equal to:

A) Price multiplied by quantity
B) Total cost divided by output
C) Marginal revenue plus price
D) Total revenue divided by quantity sold
items.correct_answer: D) Total revenue divided by quantity sold

items.prompt:
Under perfect competition, a firm's average revenue is equal to its:

A) Price (and marginal revenue)
B) Total cost
C) Fixed cost
D) Average cost only

mcq_options.text: Addition to total revenue from selling one more unit
Price of the last unit times output

items.prompt:
Marginal revenue is the:

A) Total revenue divided by quantity
B) Addition to total revenue from selling one more unit
C) Price of the last unit times output
D) Revenue left after paying costs
items.correct_answer: B) Addition to total revenue from selling one more unit

items.prompt:
A firm's profit is calculated as:

A) Total cost minus total revenue
B) Price minus average cost
C) Total revenue minus total cost
D) Total revenue plus total cost
items.correct_answer: C) Total revenue minus total cost

items.prompt:
If total revenue is N100 and total cost is N300, the firm makes a:

A) Profit of N200
B) Profit of N400
C) Loss of N400
D) Loss of N200

mcq_options.text: Total revenue just covers total cost including normal return to the entrepreneur
Total revenue is far above total cost

items.prompt:
A firm earns normal profit when:

A) Total revenue just covers total cost including normal return to the entrepreneur
B) Total revenue is far above total cost
C) Total cost exceeds revenue
D) It pays no wages
items.correct_answer: A) Total revenue just covers total cost including normal return to the entrepreneur

mcq_options.text: Total revenue exceeds total cost including normal profit

items.prompt:
Supernormal (abnormal) profit exists when:

A) Total revenue equals total cost
B) Total revenue exceeds total cost including normal profit
C) The firm makes a loss
D) Average cost equals price
items.correct_answer: B) Total revenue exceeds total cost including normal profit

items.prompt:
A profit-maximising firm produces at the output where:

A) Average cost is highest
B) Total cost is lowest
C) Marginal cost equals marginal revenue
D) Price equals fixed cost
items.correct_answer: C) Marginal cost equals marginal revenue

items.prompt:
In the short run a firm should continue to produce, even at a loss, as long as price covers at least its:

A) Average fixed cost
B) Total cost
C) Marginal cost only
D) Average variable cost

The average cost curve is typically U-shaped because of:

A) Economies then diseconomies of scale
B) Constant returns at all outputs
C) A fixed price of output
D) Government regulation
items.correct_answer: A) Economies then diseconomies of scale

items.prompt:
With total fixed cost of N100 and total variable cost of N200 at an output of 10 units, the average variable cost is:

A) N30
B) N20
C) N10
D) N200

A firm sells 50 units at N8 each. If total cost is N300, its profit is:

A) N400
B) N700
C) N100
D) N250

mcq_options.text: Many buyers and sellers of a homogeneous product

items.prompt:
A key feature of a perfectly competitive market is that there are:

A) A single seller
B) A few large sellers
C) Strong barriers to entry
D) Many buyers and sellers of a homogeneous product
items.correct_answer: D) Many buyers and sellers of a homogeneous product

items.prompt:
In perfect competition an individual firm is a price:

A) Taker
B) Maker
C) Setter
D) Leader

The demand curve facing a single firm in perfect competition is:

A) Perfectly inelastic (vertical)
B) Perfectly elastic (horizontal)
C) Downward sloping and steep
D) Upward sloping

In long-run equilibrium under perfect competition, firms earn only:

A) Supernormal profit
B) Maximum profit
C) Normal profit
D) A permanent loss

mcq_options.text: A single seller with no close substitutes

items.prompt:
A monopoly market is one in which there is:

A) Many sellers
B) A few sellers
C) Free entry of firms
D) A single seller with no close substitutes
items.correct_answer: D) A single seller with no close substitutes

items.prompt:
A monopolist's ability to set price is limited mainly by:

A) The market demand curve
B) A rival monopolist
C) Free entry of new firms
D) Government subsidy

Barriers to entry such as patents and control of raw materials help to create and sustain a:

A) Perfectly competitive market
B) Monopoly
C) Free market
D) Subsistence economy

Charging different prices to different consumers for the same product is called:

A) Price leadership
B) Predatory pricing
C) Price discrimination
D) Average cost pricing

A market with many sellers offering slightly differentiated products is called:

A) Perfect competition
B) Monopoly
C) Pure oligopoly
D) Monopolistic competition

Product differentiation in monopolistic competition is often achieved through:

A) Branding and advertising
B) Fixing one common price
C) Producing identical goods
D) Government licensing

A market dominated by a few large firms is known as an:

A) Monopoly
B) Oligopoly

items.correct_answer: D) Per capita income and life expectancy

items.prompt:
The Human Development Index (HDI) combines income with:

A) Education and life expectancy
B) Military strength
C) Exchange rates
D) The rate of inflation only

Capital formation (investment) in an economy depends largely on the level of:

A) Imports
B) Savings
C) Population growth
D) Taxation only

mcq_options.text: Shortage of capital and skilled labour

items.prompt:
Which of the following is a major obstacle to development in many developing countries?

A) Excess of capital
B) Too many engineers
C) Shortage of capital and skilled labour
D) An overdeveloped industrial base
items.correct_answer: C) Shortage of capital and skilled labour

mcq_options.text: Coordinate and direct the use of resources toward set goals

items.prompt:
Economic planning is best described as a deliberate government effort to:

A) Abolish all private firms
B) Print more money
C) Fix the weather
D) Coordinate and direct the use of resources toward set goals
items.correct_answer: D) Coordinate and direct the use of resources toward set goals

items.prompt:
A development plan that covers a period of about five years is usually called a:

A) Medium-term plan
B) Perspective plan
C) Annual budget
D) Rolling census

A major problem of development planning in many African countries is:

A) Excess skilled manpower
B) Inadequate and unreliable statistical data
C) Too much capital
D) An absence of any goals
items.correct_answer: B) Inadequate and unreliable statistical data

items.prompt:
The strategy of developing many sectors of the economy together is known as:

A) Unbalanced growth
B) Import substitution
C) Balanced growth
D) Export promotion

Financial or technical assistance given by one country to another is called:

A) Foreign trade
B) Devaluation
C) Capital flight
D) Foreign aid

A disadvantage of relying heavily on foreign loans for development is the burden of:

A) Debt servicing (repayment with interest)
B) Lower imports
C) Falling population
D) Rising exports

A development strategy that produces locally goods previously imported is called:

A) Export promotion
B) Import substitution
C) Free trade
D) Privatisation

The transfer of ownership of a public enterprise to private individuals is called:

A) Nationalisation
B) Commercialisation
C) Privatisation
D) Subsidisation

mcq_options.text: Government taking over ownership of private firms

items.prompt:
Nationalisation is the opposite of privatisation because it involves:

A) Selling public firms to citizens
B) Closing all firms
C) Reducing taxes
D) Government taking over ownership of private firms
items.correct_answer: D) Government taking over ownership of private firms

items.prompt:
The coexistence of a modern money sector and a traditional subsistence sector in one economy is called:

A) Economic dualism
B) Economic integration
C) Economic union
D) Comparative advantage

Basic facilities such as roads, electricity and water that support production are called:

A) Consumer goods
B) Infrastructure (social overhead capital)
C) Inferior goods
D) Transfer payments

mcq_options.text: Output and welfare both rise together
Output rises but the welfare of most people does not improve

items.prompt:
It is possible for a country to record economic growth without development when:

A) Output and welfare both rise together
B) Output falls
C) Output rises but the welfare of most people does not improve
D) Prices fall sharply
items.correct_answer: C) Output rises but the welfare of most people does not improve

items.prompt:
A fall in the proportion of the labour force engaged in agriculture, as industry grows, is a sign of:

A) Economic decline
B) Rising subsistence farming
C) Falling national income
D) Structural change in development

The official counting of all the people in a country at a given time is called a:

A) Census
B) Survey sample
C) Budget
D) Referendum

The natural increase in population is the difference between the:

A) Birth rate and migration
B) Birth rate and death rate
C) Death rate and emigration
D) Immigration and emigration
items.correct_answer: B) Birth rate and death rate

items.prompt:
Net migration is the difference between the number of:

A) Births and deaths
B) Males and females
C) Immigrants and emigrants
D) Adults and children

If a country has a birth rate of 40 per 1,000 and a death rate of 15 per 1,000, its rate of natural increase is:

A) 55 per 1,000
B) 15 per 1,000
C) 40 per 1,000
D) 25 per 1,000

A population with a very high proportion of young people typically has a:

A) High dependency ratio
B) Low dependency ratio
C) Falling birth rate
D) Negative growth rate

The age distribution of a population is best shown by a:

A) Demand curve
B) Population (age-sex) pyramid
C) Lorenz curve
D) Production possibility curve

mcq_options.text: Children and the aged outside the labour force

items.prompt:
The dependent population usually consists of:

A) Only factory workers
B) Only government employees
C) Children and the aged outside the labour force
D) All adult males
items.correct_answer: C) Children and the aged outside the labour force

mcq_options.text: Yields the highest output per head with available resources

items.prompt:
The optimum population of a country is the size that:

A) Is the largest possible
B) Is the smallest possible
C) Equals the labour force exactly
D) Yields the highest output per head with available resources
items.correct_answer: D) Yields the highest output per head with available resources

mcq_options.text: Too large for its resources, lowering output per head
Too small to use its resources

items.prompt:
A country is said to be overpopulated when its population is:

A) Too large for its resources, lowering output per head
B) Too small to use its resources
C) Exactly at the optimum
D) Equal to its labour force
items.correct_answer: A) Too large for its resources, lowering output per head

mcq_options.text: Too small to fully use its resources

items.prompt:
A country is said to be underpopulated when its population is:

A) Too large for its resources
B) Too small to fully use its resources
C) Exactly optimum
D) Growing too quickly
items.correct_answer: B) Too small to fully use its resources

items.prompt:
Malthus argued that population tends to grow faster than the supply of:

A) Money
B) Land area
C) Food (means of subsistence)
D) Factories

mcq_options.text: People of working age who are able and willing to work

items.prompt:
The labour force of a country consists of:

A) Everybody in the country
B) Only civil servants
C) Only the unemployed
D) People of working age who are able and willing to work
items.correct_answer: D) People of working age who are able and willing to work

mcq_options.text: Reducing per capita income and savings

items.prompt:
Rapid population growth can hinder development mainly by:

A) Reducing per capita income and savings
B) Raising per capita income
C) Removing the need for schools
D) Increasing capital per head
items.correct_answer: A) Reducing per capita income and savings

items.prompt:
An area with very many people living per square kilometre is described as:

A) Sparsely populated
B) Densely populated
C) Underpopulated
D) Optimum populated

The movement of people from rural areas to towns is called:

A) Emigration
B) Immigration
C) Rural-urban migration
D) Natural increase

mcq_options.text: A fall in demand for housing
Pressure on housing and urban unemployment

items.prompt:
A major economic effect of rural-urban migration on the cities is:

A) A fall in city population
B) An increase in farm output
C) A fall in demand for housing
D) Pressure on housing and urban unemployment
items.correct_answer: D) Pressure on housing and urban unemployment

items.prompt:
Records of births, deaths and marriages in a country are known as:

A) Vital statistics
B) National income
C) Trade statistics
D) Census errors

A major reason population censuses are difficult to conduct accurately in some developing countries is:

A) Too few people
B) Poor record-keeping and inadequate funding
C) An excess of statisticians
D) The absence of any towns
items.correct_answer: B) Poor record-keeping and inadequate funding

items.prompt:
A 'population explosion' refers to a situation where population grows:

A) Very slowly
B) At a constant low rate
C) Very rapidly, outpacing resources
D) In line with food supply

mcq_options.text: Fewer workers must support more non-workers

items.prompt:
A high dependency ratio places a burden on the working population because:

A) There are too many workers
B) Output per head rises sharply
C) Savings automatically increase
D) Fewer workers must support more non-workers
items.correct_answer: D) Fewer workers must support more non-workers

items.prompt:
A person who is able and willing to work but cannot find a job is classified as:

A) Unemployed
B) Out of the labour force
C) A dependant
D) Underemployed only

mcq_options.text: Produces all the country's crude oil
Provides food and employment for many people

items.prompt:
Agriculture remains important to the Nigerian economy mainly because it:

A) Produces all the country's crude oil
B) Provides food and employment for many people
C) Issues the national currency
D) Builds all the roads
items.correct_answer: B) Provides food and employment for many people

items.prompt:
Farming mainly to feed the farmer's own family with little left for sale is called:

A) Commercial farming
B) Plantation agriculture
C) Subsistence farming
D) Mixed farming

Large-scale farming of a single cash crop such as rubber or oil palm is called:

A) Subsistence farming
B) Shifting cultivation
C) Peasant farming
D) Plantation agriculture

mcq_options.text: Inadequate finance and poor storage facilities
An excess of fertile land used efficiently

items.prompt:
Which of the following is a major problem of agriculture in West Africa?

A) Inadequate finance and poor storage facilities
B) Too much modern machinery
C) An excess of fertile land used efficiently
D) Surplus of trained farmers
items.correct_answer: A) Inadequate finance and poor storage facilities

items.prompt:
Heavy post-harvest losses of farm produce in Nigeria are caused mainly by:

A) Excess refrigeration
B) Poor storage and processing facilities
C) Too many good roads
D) Overuse of fertiliser
items.correct_answer: B) Poor storage and processing facilities

mcq_options.text: Stabilise prices and market export crops

items.prompt:
Marketing boards were originally set up in West Africa mainly to:

A) Import manufactured goods
B) Print the currency
C) Stabilise prices and market export crops
D) Build universities
items.correct_answer: C) Stabilise prices and market export crops

items.prompt:
Which of the following was a major cash crop exported from Northern Nigeria?

A) Cocoa
B) Rubber
C) Oil palm
D) Groundnut

Cocoa was historically a leading cash crop of which part of Nigeria?

A) The South-West (Western region)
B) The far North
C) The Niger Delta only
D) The Middle Belt only

mcq_options.text: Provision of credit, improved seeds and extension services

items.prompt:
Which of the following would most help to modernise agriculture?

A) Banning all farm machinery
B) Provision of credit, improved seeds and extension services
C) Reducing rural roads
D) Stopping agricultural research
items.correct_answer: B) Provision of credit, improved seeds and extension services

mcq_options.text: Teaching improved farming methods and techniques

items.prompt:
Agricultural extension services help farmers mainly by:

A) Buying their land
B) Collecting taxes from them
C) Teaching improved farming methods and techniques
D) Fixing the exchange rate
items.correct_answer: C) Teaching improved farming methods and techniques

mcq_options.text: Increases reliance on imports of food
Creates jobs and reduces dependence on raw-material exports

items.prompt:
A major argument for industrialisation in developing countries is that it:

A) Increases reliance on imports of food
B) Lowers national income
C) Reduces employment
D) Creates jobs and reduces dependence on raw-material exports
items.correct_answer: D) Creates jobs and reduces dependence on raw-material exports

items.prompt:
Industries that extract raw materials from nature, such as mining, are called:

A) Extractive industries
B) Manufacturing industries
C) Service industries
D) Construction industries

Industries that process raw materials into finished goods are called:

A) Extractive industries
B) Manufacturing industries
C) Tertiary industries
D) Primary industries

mcq_options.text: Nearness to raw materials, power and markets

items.prompt:
Which of the following factors most influences where a manufacturing firm locates?

A) The colour of the factory
B) The age of the owner
C) Nearness to raw materials, power and markets
D) The name of the firm
items.correct_answer: C) Nearness to raw materials, power and markets

items.prompt:
A major problem facing manufacturing in Nigeria is:

A) Too much capital
B) An excess of skilled engineers
C) Surplus of cheap power
D) Inadequate and unreliable electricity supply
items.correct_answer: D) Inadequate and unreliable electricity supply

mcq_options.text: Create jobs and need less capital

items.prompt:
Small and medium-scale industries are encouraged in developing economies mainly because they:

A) Create jobs and need less capital
B) Require huge foreign loans
C) Employ very few people
D) Produce only for export
items.correct_answer: A) Create jobs and need less capital

items.prompt:
Crude oil is important to Nigeria's economy mainly as a major source of:

A) Domestic food supply
B) Government revenue and foreign exchange
C) Cheap labour
D) Agricultural land
items.correct_answer: B) Government revenue and foreign exchange

items.prompt:
Heavy dependence on crude oil exposes the Nigerian economy to the risk of:

A) Falling oil reserves only
B) A shortage of farmland
C) Fluctuations in world oil prices
D) An excess of manufactured exports
items.correct_answer: C) Fluctuations in world oil prices

mcq_options.text: Reduce over-dependence on a single commodity (oil)

items.prompt:
Economic diversification is recommended for Nigeria mainly to:

A) Increase reliance on oil
B) Stop all agriculture
C) Reduce employment
D) Reduce over-dependence on a single commodity (oil)
items.correct_answer: D) Reduce over-dependence on a single commodity (oil)

items.prompt:
The establishment of industrial estates and free-trade zones is intended to:

A) Attract investment and promote industrialisation
B) Reduce employment
C) Discourage manufacturing
D) Increase food imports
items.correct_answer: A) Attract investment and promote industrialisation

mcq_options.text: Growing crops and rearing animals on the same farm
Rearing only one type of animal

items.prompt:
Mixed farming is best described as the practice of:

A) Growing only one crop
B) Growing crops and rearing animals on the same farm
C) Rearing only one type of animal
D) Farming without any animals
items.correct_answer: B) Growing crops and rearing animals on the same farm

items.prompt:
Industrialisation can improve a country's balance of payments by:

A) Increasing imports of finished goods
B) Reducing all exports
C) Producing import-substitutes and boosting exports
D) Lowering domestic production
items.correct_answer: C) Producing import-substitutes and boosting exports
